assessment: Five-year verdict: the thesis passes. The discriminator (Melbourne, January 21, 2023) predates fame and the chase-talk pattern is dated across 2023, 2025 and 2026, in wins and losses; the draft explicitly removes the 2026 final and shows the argument standing. The hook is 2023, not the latest event. What does not yet pass is the housekeeping around the latest event and the coaching arrangement: one present-tense, uninventoried status claim carries the main evidence discount (future-01); two claims in the evidence record carry triggers that fire before publication and are still open (future-02, future-03), one of which freezes a fetch failure into the prose; and a superlative record, an undated ranking, an undated tour-landscape aside and a "still" judgment will go stale without any trigger firing (future-04, -05, -07, -08). The comparative-pain leg of the discriminator rests on the final alone (future-06); the other three legs do not. All non-stable claims in the record (C06, C36, C37, C40, C48, C60) carry actionable triggers, and the C06 podcast-date discrepancy is handled honestly by not asserting a date. The closing section is entirely 2026 US Open; that is acceptable because it is dated, framed as one more instance, and preceded by the self-test paragraph, but the editor should keep the final as a dated example rather than a culmination so a later Grand Slam title does not orphan the ending. Similarity diagnostic: not tripped per the advisory (top pair 0.055, noise-floor p99 0.008); I compared the flagged pairs against michael-jordan, Mel-Robbins and alexandr-wang and they share ordinary type vocabulary ("blind spot", "being seen to deliver") and no argument structure, so no formulaic-writing finding is warranted. Risks: contested_typing stays true (Type 3 over 7 at medium confidence); no escalation.
